items: Domain: university teacher consultation slot reservations.
Reservation: student, selected slot, title and description of the reason, and status.
User: a student creates a reservation; a teacher creates slots and approves or cancels reservations.
Operations: create a slot and reservation, approve, cancel, and check availability.
Common rule: two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot; both PENDING and CONFIRMED block the slot.
Domain rule: a slot can only be created on weekdays between 07:15 and 19:15. A student can have at most five pending reservations.
System boundary: Notification Service (still in development).
Monorepo with frontend/ and backend/ folders.
Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot and Maven.
README and documentation in docs/ exist; the repository is ready for shared work.

blocks.content: The complete Project Frame is filled in docs/intent-and-change.md. It describes the system purpose, roles, concepts, persistent state, operations, reservation state transitions, business rules, Notification Service, assumption and an open question.
Concrete future pressure at the time of C01: after a request is submitted, the teacher must make a separate decision; the reservation must not be confirmed automatically on creation.

Why it is relevant: this requirement changes the reservation lifecycle, availability rules, teacher authorization, audit history and user interface. It was future pressure in C01; C02 adopted baseline v0.2, and the current system implements it with PENDING and teacher approval to CONFIRMED.

Tasks follow the team workflow. One team member implements a change in their own branch, another member reviews it in a pull request, and the change is merged into main after approval. The review verifies functionality, readability, project rules and conflicts.

We verified real reservation persistence in PostgreSQL. Docker Compose runs the database, backend and frontend; Flyway creates the schema and demo data at startup. The backend reads slots through the REST API and data can be verified in the database.

items: Evidence: compose.yaml, DOCKER.md and Flyway migrations in backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/.
Result: availability is protected by both the backend and database constraints, so two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot.

blocks.content: Evidence is documented in docs/evidence-and-evolution.md: the question verified PostgreSQL reads and writes; Docker Compose was used for the run; Flyway migrations and visible demo slots were observed. Decision: PostgreSQL, Flyway and Docker Compose remain the standard for local startup and database schema management.
POST /api/reservations → validation → persist to PostgreSQL → 201 Created with reservation ID → automated integration check. The definition is in README.md.

The reservation domain, Resource / Reservation / User model, states, operations, rules, system boundary, Project Frame, selected future pressure, review workflow, engineering spike, evidence and CP1 skeleton are described and evidenced.
